The submitted request sets out the following key components of the activity: a) A processing capacity to produce up to 6000 tonnes annually. 2000 tonnes of marc will be sent directly from the winery off site as stock feed during vintage and the remaining 3000-4000 tonnes of grape marc would provide the base feedstock of the soil conditioner/compost. B) The facility will use marc exclusively from the Yealands Estate Limited operation. It is not intended that the composting will be a commercial activity providing a disposal point for grape marc for the wider industry. C) The composting process is to be undertaken within a large building to provide a controlled environment and avoid stormwater contact with marc causing environmental issues. D) The building will sit on an impermeable concrete floor with liquid from the marc piles being caught in a series of channels and directed to holding tanks. E) Tank volumes will be monitored frequently and additional tanks are available from the winery if required so that no overflows occur. F) Liquid will be required to keep the compost in a suitable moisture range to allow optimal compositing conditions. Through recirculation and evapotranspiration, the quality of liquid in the storage tanks will be managed on site. G) No liquid discharge to land or water will occur from the marc piles or composting process. With recirculation, it will instead be a closed system.

The applicants are currently building a house on Lot 2 DP 396001 under Building Consent BC191544 and Resource Consent U180902.2. The Resource Consent allowed for excavation and filling with Condition 1 of the resource consent being “The development shall be undertaken in accordance with the application documents received by Council on 26 October and further information received on 23 November 2018 and 7 December 2018, held on Marlborough District Council electronic file U180902.” Any suitable excavated material (weathered rock) has been used to fill behind the retaining wall and any fill not required to fill behind the retaining wall was to be taken off site. But in the end, while some rock was placed, additional greywache hardfill was imported and placed, being a more reliable and suitable fill for a driveway. However, instead of taking the excess fill off site, the applicants and contractor decided to place the fill on site, which is different to the development shown on the documents supplied and approved under U180902, and therefore non-compliant with Condition 1. The bulk of the property is in the Sounds Residential Zone with the northern area adjacent to Lot 1 DP 396001 and Lot 3 DP 1156 being in Rural 1 Zone in the Marlborough Sounds Resource Management Plan (MSRMP).

The car parking configuration referenced in the original resource consent was based on an earlier site plan, which included six (6) parking spaces arranged in a specific layout. Since then, a new and improved site plan has been developed, featuring a more accessible and efficient parking design. We request that condition 4 on U190797 be updated to refer to this revised layout rather than the outdated version. The updated site plan, as referenced in Condition 4, still provides six (6) parking spaces. However, the configuration has been enhanced to improve manoeuvrability and accessibility. All six spaces are now arranged in a single line, which simplifies vehicle movement and maximises usable space. The new layout also includes a dedicated accessible (disability) parking space. While the total number of parking spaces remains unchanged, the revised configuration offers a more practical and user-friendly design.

Proposal To construct and use autility building (to house a substation), having a gross floor area exceeding65 square metres on Lot 6 DP 342799. They request a 10 year lapse date (instead of the default 5 years provided for in the RMA). Lapse Date A 10 year lapse date is considered appropriate for a building to house a substation and given the applicant's role as network utility operator responsible for ensuring an uninterrupted electrical supply for local residents and businesses. The supply of electricity is a long-term activity with long lead times to design and commission new facilities such the one proposed here. Large users can dominate the demand profile. Demand can jump quickly with large users requesting significant increases in load in very short timeframes. There are some current examples of this with large winery expansions. In addition, optimisation of the network is a complex matter and to do it efficiently requires good long term planning. To cope with this pattern of use and to allow MLL to meet customers' expectations MLL policy is to have as much pre-planning completed as possible. Approval to build this type of facility is part of that process. There are also benefits for the residents of the locality as MLL has signalled well in advance what its plans are. This will allow them to accurately manage their overall strategy with regard to security of supply and future upgrades as they can be sure this facility can be built when needed. While the District Plan does have provisions that facilitate the creation of substations it is in everyone's interest to have these matters settled well in advance. In this regard, the applicant advises: “We have an important role to distribute electricity to our customers and that demand can change very quickly with one large customer exiting or entering the network. We are continuously monitoring demand for when this substation will be needed.” Electricity distribution is tricky to predict, and many factors can affect the supply and demand experienced in the market at any given time. Large users can dominate the demand profile and demand can jump quickly with large users requesting significant increases in load in very short timeframes. The growth Marlborough Lines predicted and experienced on its network over the last five years was less than anticipated and as such, our existing infrastructure was able to cope with those increases without the need to exercise consent U160053 for a new substation. Despite the rate of growth being slower than predictions, long term planning still expects growth and at which time Marlborough Lines' existing infrastructure is nearing capacity, we would exercise this consent. Due to the unpredictable nature of the industry and to assist in long term planning, Marlborough Lines would like to extend the lapse date of consent U160053 for a further ten years out to 2031. This would provide certainty that an option is there ready at the time the market needs the additional infrastructure in its electricity distribution. There is no intention to alter any other aspect of the consent at this time. Marlborough Lines' customers trust us to supply consistent electricity to their homes and businesses in the safest manner. Through extending the lapse period of this consent for a further ten years, it gives us the best opportunity to pre-plan and put our customers first to ensure their homes and businesses keep running uninterrupted.” We assess that the longer lapse date sought is also supported by the MEP's objectives and policies, which recognise importance of regionally significant infrastructure and the contribution it makes to the region's social and economic wellbeing. Alzheimers Society Marlborough Inc, has been providing services to the community for over 30 years. They operate from a purpose-built facility on a Council site at the corner of Wither and Taylor Pass Roads which has a vehicle entrance at 8 Wither Road. They wish to expand their premises, and the expansion includes a secondary access off Taylor Pass Road. Resource consent is needed for the proposed new vehicle crossing, as it does not meet the permitted setback from the intersection of Taylor Pass Road with Wither Road. This application is for authorisation of the proposed new vehicle crossing location. The proposal is to install a 4 to 6m wide vehicle crossing on the Taylor Pass Road frontage of Lot 1 DP 329656. As shown on the attached Plan, SP2 ‘Proposed Vehicle Crossing Position' the proposed crossing location is: 12.5m from the intersection on the opposite side of the road (where a 20m setback applies); and 35.6m from the intersection on the same side of the road (where a 40m setback applies). The crossing location is on a straight section of Taylor Pass Road with a 50 km/hour speed limit. The proposed crossing will meet other relevant permitted standards: its width will be between 4m and 9m (2.33.4.2); a 15m separation from other crossings is achieved (2.33.4.16); it is within the maximum of two crossings on this road frontage (2.33.4.18); and an 80m minimum sight distance is available (2.33.4.19). In addition, the layout for the expanded Alzheimers Society premises will be such that vehicles will enter and exit the premises in a forward-facing direction onto Taylor Pass Road.

Discharge a maximum of 840 litre per day of treated domesticeffluent to land via drip irrigation. Wastewater Revalidation The original one bedroom bach with separate bunk room was upgraded in 2010- 2012 Dwelling Alterations / Extensions - PIM Issued PIM090845(see property files) The wastewater management system was also upgraded at this time with a design flow for a three bedroom (6 people) house with 840 litres/day and an on site secondary treatment wastewater system consisting of a KiwiTreat system with treatment pumped to 251 metres of driplines. The system was the last building activity completed and was activated and commissioned February 2012. On the expiry of the current consent the components of the systems that have not been replaced will have been used for only 12 years and 9 months. A maintenance and service log book has been kept and is available to view if required. Photos and small videos of servicingof the system are available to view if required. In 2020 a Notice To Fix and Abatement Notice was issued. All technical non compliance issues were remedied and the notice was liftedand remedied as part ofCOA 200040.(see property file) At this time the drip line was extended to294metres with the addition of an air release valve and an additional flush valve. Morgan Plumbing examined and reported on the system. (Report attached.) The wastewater management system has been assessed against the current codes, AS/NZS 1547:2012 and local best practice. The assessment has found that a three-bedroom house with water conserving fixtures and no bath requires a 257 metre dripline. A risk assessment has been undertaken which has determined that the system has LOW risk of causing any short or long-term environmental issues. The site investigation and assessment concluded that the system complies with current codes and is low risk. (Attached) Current good practice is to have a ‘Loading Certificate' on display somewhere prominent in the house. This summarises the wastewater system for the property and reminds occupants, particularly visitors, about the limitations of it.( A copy is attached.) Consents Required The proposal will require a Discharge Permit to continue to use the existing on-site wastewater system. This is a Discretionary Activity in terms of the MEP.

Removing or replacing fuel storage system (1) Removing or replacing a fuel storage system is a permitted activity while the following requirements are met: (a) the activity must be done in accordance with the current edition ofGuidelines for Assessing and Managing Petroleum Hydrocarbon Contaminated Sites in New Zealand, Wellington, Ministry for the Environment: (b) the territorial authority of the district where the system is located must be notified of— (i) the place where the activity is to be done: (ii) the dates on which it is intended that the activity begin and end: (iii) the facility at which it is intended that soil taken away in the course of the activity be disposed of: (c) notification under paragraph (b) must be done no sooner than 1 month and no later than 1 week before the activity begins: (d) the volume of soil disturbed must be no more than 30m3for each tank in the system: (e) the volume of soil taken away in the course of the activity must be no more than 30 m3for each tank in the system: (f) soil taken away in the course of the activity must be disposed of at a facility authorised to receive soil of that kind: (g) the duration of the activity must be no longer than 2 months: (h) the results of the investigation of the piece of land required by the guidelines described in paragraph (a) must be reported to the territorial authority within 3 months after the activity ends.

It is proposed to realign MFL189/U090242 & MPE408/U071125 (6.03 ha) being marine farm site 8552 in Clova Bay, Pelorus Sound. To enable the continuing cultivation of Green Shell Mussels (Perna canaliculus), Blue Shell Mussels (Mytilus galloprovincialis), Flat Oysters (Tiostrea lutaria) and Scallops (Pecten novaezelandiae) and naturally settled seaweed and algae species (Macrocystis pyrifera, Ecklonia radiata, Gracilaria, Pterocladia lucida). The farm remains at 6.03 hectares with 17 longlines in two blocks. Back bone length is 2248m with the 157m loss made up on MF8557. The proposal follows the MDC Variation 1 Panel's decision for the site. Consent is also sought to disturb the seabed with anchoring devices and to harvest marine farming produce including taking and discharge of coastal seawater and discharge biodegradable and organic waste matter during harvest. Length of term requested is to 2040. An election under the RM (Extended Duration of Coastal Permits for Marine Farms) Amendment Act 2024 was made and confirmed. Existing consents will be surrendered.

The applicants wish to construct a new deck on the western side of the building to provide outdoor seating for customers to the restaurant/bar. The deck will be constructed at the floor level of the mezzanine floor approximately 3m above the ground floor of the building and 1.7m above the top of the stop bank.The deckwill provide an outdoor seating area for the restaurant/bar. Resource ConsentU240672.01 Condition 3. states"The activity shall take place entirely within the existing building and no outdoor seating shall be established unless authorized by further resource consent approval." Therefore a land use resource consentis required to use the new deck as an outdoor seating area. The deck will be 9m x 4m and feature a timber deck on 450mm diameter concrete columns. The foundation for the deck will be located on the stopbank of the Taylor River on engineer designed foundations. The use of bored pile foundations is recommended. To ensure the structural integrity of the stop bank, the foundation piles must be placed below the base of the stop bank.The construction methodology involves drilling a circular hole into the ground using a rotary rig, then installing steel reinforcement and filling the bore with concrete to create a strong, cast-in-place deep foundation. Foundations for the deck will be 600mm diameter concrete foundations to approximately3m deep anda 600mm x 600mm foundation beam. A site plan and building plans of the proposed deck are provided as an attachment. An Geotechnical Report (Geotechnical Report, Feast Merchants,13 Grove Road, Blenheim,September 2025 issue: 02 Our Ref: 9298)is included as an attachment.
Rory Alan King, Frances Peita King

The Applicant intendsto carrying out renovations to the function room to create a one bedroom unit with ensuite and kitchenette. The unit will be used by family members and the applicants also wish to use the unit for commercial visitor accommodation at times. The proposal involves alterations tothe internal layout of the building to convert it to be fit for purpose for visitor accommodation. Building consent will be required for the proposedinternal changes. A Site Plan and proposed Floor Plan are provided as an attachment. Ample parking is available on site, with two dedicated parking spaces provided for guests of the accommodation unit. Guests will access the unit via the vehicle crossing on Hammerichs Road, which enters Lot 1 DP 5711 and serves as the site ingress. The vehicle crossing located on the southern boundary of Part Lot 2 DP 5711 is used solely for vehicle egress. The proposal does not require and signage, however if signage is to occur in the future it would be in accordance with signage rules for the Rural Environment Zone. The applicants intend on converting the existing cafe/restaurant into a 4 bedroom dwelling which is a Permitted Activity. The proposed dwelling and one-bedroom accommodation unit will be serviced by the existing on-site wastewater treatment and disposal system. An assessment undertaken by Smart Alliances Ltdconfirms that the system was installed in 2020 by Findlater Construction Ltd and comprises a 5,000-litre grease trap, a Findlater A5000 secondary treatment unit, and 1,400 m² of pressurised dripline disposal area configured as two separate 700 m² fields. The system was designed by Smart Alliances Ltd to accommodate a daily wastewater flow of up to 4,900 litres. The conversion of the two existing buildings will generate an equivalent wastewater load of five bedrooms. Using a conservative design assumption of two occupants per bedroom and a wastewater generation rate of 200 litres per person per day, the maximum daily wastewater discharge is estimated to be 2,000 litres per day (10 persons × 200 litres/person/day). As the estimated wastewater load is substantially below the system's design capacity, the existing wastewater treatment and disposal system is considered more than adequate to service the proposed dwelling and accommodation unit. A copy of the wastewater assessment prepared by Smart Alliances Ltd is provided as an attachment (ref:11176-LTR-ww-01).

The Kutai Guy Limited proposes to operate a mussel processing, smoking and packaging business within the existing purpose-built seafood processing and export facility at 2 Rangitane Drive, Havelock, formerly occupied by Cloudy Bay Clams. Activities will include receiving and refrigerated storage of live green-lipped mussels, grading and repacking live mussels, cooking, shelling, brining, hot smoking, cooling, vacuum packaging, freezing, cold storage and dispatch for domestic and export markets. The cooker and smokehouse are electrically heated. A separate smoke generator supplies wood smoke for flavouring, with smokehouse exhaust discharged through a flue proposed through the roof. The flue will be designed and installed in accordance with the manufacturer's requirements and any applicable consent conditions. The operation will use the existing building, processing areas, refrigeration facilities, yard access and loading areas. Associated activities include deliveries, product collection, equipment cleaning and waste handling. Shell and organic processing waste will be collected in bins, held under chilled conditions and removed regularly. Trade waste arrangements for the proposed operation have already been established with Marlborough District Council. Process wastewater will be managed in accordance with the applicable trade waste approval and its conditions. The proposal will reuse a facility specifically built for seafood processing and export, supporting local employment and adding value to New Zealand green-lipped mussels.

The Blenheim to Stoke A 110 kV (hereafter referred to as BLN-STK A) line follows a route from the Stoke Substation, up the Matai River Valley, through the Maungatapu Saddle, down the Pelorus River Valley, around the hills 1 kilometre to the south of Canvastown, down the Kaituna River Valley to cross the Wairau River to the north of Renwick and turns at the refuse tip to run along the north side of Old Renwick Road to the Blenheim Substation. The towers are numbered from 1 at the Blenheim end to 203 at the Stoke end.
